items.note: Story 1: LVCCA organized 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery 1891, Gideon Vose first president.
Gives payment by butterfat test not weight, but never states the second bolded element, 'the test of the station where he delivers governs'.
Story 1: 'under payment by weight, none of what follows would have cost anyone a dollar'.
Teague (bookkeeper) and Sill (buttermaker) appear, but Effie Loomis, secretary and keeper of the minute book, is never mentioned anywhere in the answers.
Son of Gideon is right, but Story 5 says 'manager from 1911' (r23's date-drift error); key requires 1913.

Story 2 describes the annual 'station gain' line, credited vs arrived butterfat, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual'; Story 6 says arrivals exceeded credits. The 1898 origin is not stated, but it is unbolded.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896; first-season glass borrowed (Sill's, and 'done borrowing of Larrow Green').
Section A never describes weighing, composite samples, the percent-graduated neck or the fixed pipette charge (the neck mechanism appears only in C1a and F1).
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight; $77.93.
Story 2: 'a flat 0.19 points, holding steady across every month and season, in winter and summer alike'.
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and that the county had none.
Keddie tester from opening, twenty-nine seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 7).
The station test book in Keddie's hand is named (Stories 3 and 7). Bolded element present; the column detail is unbolded context.
Summary leaf not given: no 1896 recorded average of 3.80 against 3.61 from 1898. The 3.80 in Section A is only the corrected true average, not the 1896 season on borrowed glass.

Story 3: broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure until 10 July, nine weeks, tests rose and fell back the day own glass resumed, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing, but the item has no REQUIRED line and the core fact is present.
Story 5: 'Orra's brother Emmet Brant, the largest Hessel Bottom patron' confronted Ansel; Orra is shown as Ansel's wife via the household/diary (Stories 1, 7).
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are is absent; both bolded elements required.
Story 7: died in 1934 with the accusation unresolved.
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Brant's weigh book mentioned only as an exhibit; no 1 January 1897 start and no statement that the two scales agreed.
1902 complaints present; 3.61 vs Larrow Green 3.78 given, and 0.19 kept as the recorded-vs-true gap. No 0.19 Hollow-vs-Green conflation found.
Grigg committee sampled January-March 1908 only, 'concluded that wet hay was the cause', reported as the committee's finding and refuted.
Brant's 1910 200,000 lb at 3.42 and the proportional loss (Vose Jerseys 4.56) are absent from Section A (1910 figures appear only in C2).
No custody chain: Roy Brant 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel after 1962.
Only 'the Alder Corners cheese factory (over the ridge)'; no Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd.
Story 4: the same four Hessel Bottom farms hauled there in summer, 1915-1930.
No independence elements (other county, bench, glassware, uncompared book). At most the artifact ('Rosalie Cudd's Alder Corners records') counts as one of the two required.
Same four farms tested 3.78-3.82 there across sixteen summers 1915-1930, against the station's 3.61, i.e. about 0.19 higher.
Same farms' milk tested differently at two stations; 'the deficiency traveled with the Ostrey Hollow station, not with the hay or the cows'.
Rosalie Cudd named only as a source; no 'daughter', no 1941-1962, no copying sixteen seasons for Ivy in 1958.
Merle Strawn named, but his circuit is dated 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23/X102); key requires 1907-1936.
Story 5: lactometer at every circuit visit 'never once found added water at the station'.
Ran pipettes against a calibrated burette; condemned the entire lot 12 June 1923.
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Says the recorded average 'immediately rose to 3.85% and held there'; key requires 3.80 (3.85 is r22's planted error). Also no 28 June / 2 July dates.
Crate to the loft is given, but the second bolded element, notebooks to the college library in 1947, is absent.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Board chaired by Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, two of three sittings at the station.
Heard watering, skimming, wet hay; found none proven.
Four exhibits listed including the inspector's 1923 notebook, but not that it contained the answer and was read for its other lines (bolded).
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no theory proven; award $3,800 'without admission' four days later.
Section A gives neither the one-fifth of $19,000 nor that the award was charged to the station account where the gain accumulated.
Granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, with Professor Leland Vaught.
No statement in Section A that she assembled records never before in one room.
February 1958, crate found (in the loft where it was forgotten), nine surviving pipettes.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, 16.72 against 17.6, 'about 5% short'.
Recorded 3.61, true 3.80, flat 0.19 gap, glass in use 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923.
Section A has no 40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 or ledger-identity statement (all appear only in Section C).
Bulletin No. 471 October 1958 and 'twenty-four years after his death' present; 33 years after the dismissal absent, so the bolded interval set is incomplete.
Granddaughter.
Derived from Duncan being Ansel's son and Ivy Duncan's daughter; notes r22's self-correction.
Second cousins, with the siblings-first cousins-children derivation.
Abstention item A08: never raises the full vs half sibling question; says the sources 'leave nothing substantial open'. No assertion either way, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose; rejects the 'nephew' rumor.
Significance given as 'institutional insider by birth'; does not connect Gideon's Article VII making the test decisive, nor the Vose Jerseys as largest loser.

Abstention item A01: 'The sources do not establish any real connection' and 'the documents cannot fully prove the absence of one'. No verdict that they were or were not kin, so under the operational test it counts as an abstention.
Does not state that no document names or denies a link or that a family denial is not a record; instead weighs Duncan's denial as the best-positioned evidence.
True 3.60, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed.

$90.00 at 25 cents, explicitly flagged as the period-average price with working shown. This meets the key's acceptance condition, though the claim that no 1910 price exists is wrong (r09 gives 24 cents).
76,000 lb; 5.26% of credited and 5.00% of delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 by itemized addition.
72 pipettes, each 0.88 c.c. short.
Gives '26 calendar years' for the glass (and 'parts of 27 calendar years'), not the exact 26 years and 6 weeks; exact-match section.
Abstention item A02: asserts 'an estimated 1,100,000 lb' (r23's pole) as the answer; the hedge follows a verdict sentence. -2 applied.
Variable: the measuring instrument, own glass vs borrowed, 8 May-10 July.
Tester, herds, pasture, season held constant.
Only 'rose... fell back to their former level'; no 3.80 through the interval and 3.61 on return.
Cause tracked the instrument, not cows, calendar or tester; limit: no size in c.c. measured in 1911.
1911 interval (r22, r24), ledger surplus (r05, r14, r23), Alder Corners (r10): three reasons from at least three narrators.
Argues independence by evidence body; names the ledger surplus as surviving without 1958.
Abstention item A09: 'On the substance, though: no', resting on Kyle's pole. -2 applied.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low; cites the 1919 circular.
Only two of five: signed the sheets and wrote the 1919 circular. Manager given as 1911 (wrong); no watering argument at the hearing attributed to him; the silence on glass/pipette is never noted.

Abstention item A03: says only 'no clear evidence of awareness'; no declared inability to settle it, and none of the required observations (it takes Kyle's pole as evidence instead). No verdict sentence, so no deduction.

Right value found with a method but the pair not noticed: 16.72 vs r11's 16.27 (arithmetic), $3,800 vs r21's $3,500 (document-based accounts), 3.61 vs r13's 3.16. None of the key's ordinary table rows are resolved correctly: it takes 3.85 for the 1924 average, 1911 for Selby, and leans toward eleven families.

Pairs named with breakers: NT-10 (1898, r11 and r23; broken by the dated invoice), NT-11 (12 July, r08 and r12; broken by Strawn's own account), NT-14 ($77.39, r19 and r20; broken by the itemized addition), NT-22 (two tenths, r15 and r16; broken by quoted D12), NT-18, NT-5. Capped at 3.
None of A04, A06 or A10 is raised.
Self-contradictions flagged (r20's $77.39 total, r16's 0.20/0.21, r12's and r22's late reversals, r14) are not among the key's nine catalogued internal contradictions.

1897 pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, proportional 5%, 0.19 = 5% of 3.80, onset 1897 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing on the farms changing. The 1924 '3.85' is an unbolded context element and is charged as a deduction instead.
Watering (Vose) defeated by the inspector's lactometer never finding water.
Theft defeated by cream arriving heavier than credited, plus the 1911 interval.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter/none summer vs a flat 0.19, plus Alder Corners.
Abstention item A07: 'The 1925 board of arbitration never examined the condemned glassware', asserted (also repeated in G). -2 applied.
Abstention item A05: 'The tester himself privately believed... that the cause was something in the glass', asserted from r18's pole. -2 applied.
Summary is about 167 words, over the 150-word limit.
Only about four of the nine series (ledgers, invoice, hearing record, 1958 measurement); 'diaries', 'scientific claims' and 'family memory' are not keyed series.
No decoy adopted and no wrong headline figure in the summary.
About 5% low, 1897, loft since 1923, 1958: four elements covering both ends (names absent).

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (r23 X94), asserted in Story 5 and D3
Corruption: 1924 station average 3.85 (r22 X90), asserted in Story 8, C1b and F1
Corruption: Strawn's lactometer/circuit 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23, r22 X102), asserted in Story 5 and F2
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake asserted as 1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A09: asserts the bookkeeper never questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A07: asserts the board never examined the glassware (F, G)
Gullibility A05: asserts the tester believed it was the glass (F)
